judged_text: In updateEvent, when the reference's credentialId is not in this.calendarCredentials and the DB lookup returns nothing, `updateEvent(credential, ...)` is still called with credential undefined, unlike createAllCalendarEvents which guards with `if (credential)`. The undefined credential reaches CalendarManager's getCalendar/credential destructuring and throws a TypeError; the surrounding catch then returns success:false for every calendar reference, so one stale/missing credential (e.g. a deleted teammate credential on a collective booking) marks all calendar updates as failed instead of skipping the one dead reference.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` within the calendar-update flow (the function that builds `calendarReference` as an array and then `for (const reference of calendarReference)`), when `reference.credentialId` is present the code sets `credential` from `this.calendarCredentials`, optionally tries a DB lookup if not found, but then unconditionally does `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId));` even if `credential` is still `undefined` (e.g., DB lookup returns null). This differs from `createAllCalendarEvents`, which guards with `if (credential)`. The outer `try/catch` around the whole function would then catch the thrown error and return a failure result for all references (`calendarReference?.map(...)`), matching the finding’s described failure mode.
